newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand shares close softer, trade narrowly.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand shares close softer, trade narrowly.

text.p: * New Zealand shares close marginally weaker
* Fletcher Building jumps on Manapouri contract win
* Turnover low, leaders trade narrow band
Price movements at close
LAST CHG
333 -1 * NZSC cap index -1.76 at 5,107.55
373 -2 * Volume NZ$33.6million. Futures untraded
698 -2 * Other movers - +10 +10
New Zealand shares closed a fraction lower in light trading on Monday, with a 10 cent rise in Fletcher Building shares the only highlight, brokers said.
A consortium led by Fletcher Building announced it had won a NZ$200 million contract to tunnel a second tailrace for the Manapouri hydro-electric scheme in New Zealand's South Island.
"It was a pretty quiet all round with the index trading in a narrow range all day with few bright spots," broker David Fear of County Natwest said.
The NZSE40 capital index shed 1.99 points to close at 2,330.28 after trading between 2334 and 2325 on the day.

"Fletcher Building was the highlight, closing up 10 cents on the back of the Manapouri contract. Details are a litle bit scarce at this stage but it just goes to show that Fletcher Building is well positioned in New Zealand to win some of these major contracts."
He said major contracts in power generation, water, sewage, roading and transport would come through later in the year and Fletcher had good potential to win them.
Carter Holt Harvey had a mixed day ahead of its December quarter result due on Tuesday. Fear said the market was picking earnings of between $62 million and $75 million.
Brokers said the market would be watching with interest a breakfast meeting on Tuesday featuring Treasurer Winston Peters and Prime Minister Jim Bolger to see how they were working together.
The conservative National Party and Peters' New Zealand First Party formed a coalition government after last October's general election.
"People will want to see what sort of dialogue they have together and how they come across as a combined unit," Fear said.
